name: ReferenceGenome
description: ONGA descriptor schema for the reference genome a track is defined against (FGA-issue-adjacent: every genomic annotation is relative to a reference assembly). Carries content-derived seqcol digests and human-readable identifiers for the exact assembly, plus the sex of the reference build (factored out of compound terms like "male genome reference"). The build sex is a property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample (that is Donor.donor_sex). Absorbs the FGA-WG GenomeAssembly class.

slots.name: seqcol_digest
slots.description: Top-level sequence collection digest according to the GA4GH refget, Sequence Collections standard (v1.0). This a globally unique identifier for the genome assembly, algorithmically derivable from the genome assembly content. Usage is to uniquely identify the exact genome assembly used and allow detailed comparisons across genome assembly variants (say, variants of the GRCh38 assembly).

slots.name: accessions
slots.description: Database accession numbers for the genome assembly, if available. Should precisely identify the genome assembly and be omitted if changes have been made to the assembly after retrieval, such as removing the alternate sequences.

slots.name: aliases
slots.description: Human-readable aliases of the genome assembly. Can be imprecise, as preciseness is enforced in the other fields.

slots.name: build_sex
slots.description: The sex of the reference genome build (which sex chromosomes the assembly contains). Factored out of compound DataType terms like "male genome reference" / "female genome index". A property of the reference assembly, NOT of the biological sample. Absent means unspecified / sex-neutral combined assembly.

slots.name: seqcol_ordered_coord_system
slots.description: Content-derived digest that uniquely identifies the ordered coordinate system of the genome assembly. (Coordinate systems with the same sequence names and lengths, but where the sequences are ordered differently, will have different ordered digests.). Usage is the ordered coordinate system digest can be used to uniquely generate a chromSizes file, useful in a number of analysis tools. Definition is the ordered coordinate system digest is defined as the level 1 digest of the name_length_pairs attribute of the sequence collection generated from the genome assembly.

slots.name: seqcol_unordered_coord_system
slots.description: Content-derived digest that uniquely identifies the order-invariant coordinate system of the genome assembly. This digest will be shared across all coordinate systems with the same sequence names and lenghts, regardless of the order of the sequences. Usage is the order-invariant coordinate system digest can be used to uniquely describe the coordinate system of a particular genome browser instance and the annotation files that are compatible with it. Definition is the order-invariant coordinate system digest is defined as the level 1 digest of the sorted_name_length_pairs attribute of the sequence collection generated from the genome assembly.

name: TrackFormat
description: How a genomic annotation file is encoded: its primary file format and, for BED-family formats, the number of standard (core) and extra (custom) columns. Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #1.

slots.name: file_format
slots.description: The primary file format in which the track is encoded.

slots.name: bed_core_columns
slots.description: For BED-family formats, the number of standard (core) BED columns present — the N in "BEDN". Only relevant when file_format is a BED-family format.

slots.name: bed_extra_columns
slots.description: For BED-family formats, the number of extra/custom columns appended after the core columns — the M in "BEDN+M". Only relevant when file_format is a BED-family format.

name: TrackGeometry
description: Overall geometric properties of the sequence features in the genomic annotation file if considered as an one-dimensional genome browser track, in line with the track type delineations from Gundersen et. al, 2011. While conceptually based on visual characteristics, these properties are also useful to e.g. select relevant annotation files for non-visual analyses.

rules.summary: When has_lengths is true: lengths_constant required.
When has_values is true: value_type required.
When has_edges is true: edges_have_weights, edges_are_directed, edges_denote_parents required.
When edges_have_weights is true: edge_weight_type required.

slots.name: elements_circular
slots.description: Whether the sequence features have circular coordinates (at least one feature that cross a sequence border).

slots.name: elements_overlapping
slots.description: Whether the sequence features are overlapping (at least one base pair is simultaneously covered by two sequence features).

slots.name: has_edges
slots.description: Whether the sequence features are linked across positions (at least one edge between features exists).

slots.name: has_gaps
slots.description: Whether there are gaps between the sequence features (there exists at least one gap between two features on the same sequence).

slots.name: has_lengths
slots.description: Whether the sequence features have lengths (at least one feature spans more than 1 base pair).

slots.name: has_names
slots.description: Whether the sequence features are named (at least one feature has a name).

slots.name: has_strands
slots.description: Whether the sequence features are stranded (at least one feature has strand information).

slots.name: has_values
slots.description: Whether the sequence features have associated values (at least one feature has an associated value).

slots.name: edge_weight_type
slots.description: The type of values associated with the edges.

slots.name: edges_are_directed
slots.description: Whether the edges linking sequence features are directed (at least one edge between sequence features is defined with a direction).

slots.name: edges_denote_parents
slots.description: Whether the edges linking sequence features denote a parent-child relationship (all edges between sequence features denote parent-child relationships such as genes to exons, i.e. where the child is fully covered by the parent).

slots.name: edges_have_weights
slots.description: Whether the edges linking sequence features are weighted (at least one edge between sequence features has an associated weight).

slots.name: lengths_constant
slots.description: Whether the sequence lengths are constant (all sequence features have the same length, excluding features at the very end of a sequence).

slots.name: value_type
slots.description: The type of values associated with the sequence features, if any.

name: TrackInterpretation
description: What the data in a genomic annotation file represents, split into an algorithmic interpretation (output_type, drawing on the DataType vocabulary) and a biological interpretation (feature_type, drawing on the FeatureType vocabulary). Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #2.

slots.name: element_type
slots.description: The Sequence Ontology class(es) that the individual rows/records of this track instantiate. One value = a homogeneous set; several values = a mixed set (rows may be instances of any listed class); absent = the rows are not SO-typeable features (signal values, matrices, models, edges). This is a CONTENT facet — it answers *what the rows are* — so it lives on TrackInterpretation, not TrackProvenance (design principle #4). It is the slot form of the `onga:has_element_type` relation: an ONGA term denotes a SET of elements, an SO class denotes the element type, and ONGA never asserts equivalence between them (design principle #7).

slots.name: feature_type
slots.description: The biological interpretation: the biological entity or concept the data represents (e.g. TF binding site, enhancer, CpG island). Draws on the FeatureType vocabulary.

slots.name: haplotype_resolution
slots.description: The haplotype resolution the file represents: whether content is resolved to individual alleles (allele_specific), partitioned per parental haplotype (haplotype_specific), or phase-resolved without per-haplotype splitting (phased). A content facet factored out of compound DataType/FeatureType terms (e.g. "haplotype-specific contact matrix", "phased variant calls"). Absent means haplotype-collapsed / not phase-resolved.

slots.name: output_type
slots.description: The algorithmic interpretation: the computational process or output the file represents (e.g. peaks, signal, alignment, count matrix). Draws on the DataType vocabulary.

slots.name: strand
slots.description: The strand orientation the file represents. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "minus strand signal"). Absent means unstranded/unspecified.

name: TrackProvenance
description: The processing/derivation operations applied to the data to produce the file: which read subset it was computed from (read_multiplicity), what QC filtering operation was applied (filter_status), and what scaling normalization was applied (normalization), what retention cut / thresholding was applied (thresholding), and the epistemic origin of the values (derivation: observed vs. predicted). This schema is the planned home for further processing facets as they are decided. Boundary with the Analysis record class (Layer 4): TrackProvenance carries faceted, closed-vocabulary descriptors of what was done to the CONTENT; Analysis is the record of the ACTIVITY itself (workflow, tool, version, inputs). Complementary, not competing.

slots.name: derivation
slots.description: The epistemic origin of the file's values (observed vs predicted) — whether they were empirically measured from experimental data or generated by a computational/statistical model. Factored out of compound DataType / FeatureType terms (e.g. "observed signal profile", "predicted signal profile", "predicted transcription start sites"). `control` is excluded: it denotes an experimental role or normalization reference, not the measured-vs-model axis. Absent means unspecified (not a default of observed).

slots.name: filter_status
slots.description: The quality-control filtering operation applied (filtered vs unfiltered). Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "filtered peaks", "unfiltered alignments"). Absent means unspecified.

slots.name: normalization
slots.description: The scaling normalization applied to a signal (raw vs depth-normalized vs percentage-normalized) — the scaling operation applied. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "raw signal", "normalized signal", "percentage normalized signal"). Does not cover statistic transforms (p-value, fold-change, z-score, enrichment) or smoothing, which are distinct output_types. Absent means unspecified (not raw).

slots.name: read_multiplicity
slots.description: The read mapping-multiplicity subset the data was computed from (all mapped reads vs uniquely-mapping reads only) — the read-selection operation applied. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "signal of all reads"). Absent means unspecified.

slots.name: thresholding
slots.description: The retention cut / thresholding operation applied to produce the file, and its basis (idr vs mapping_quality vs significance). Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "IDR thresholded peaks", "mapping quality thresholded contact matrix"). Cross-cuts peaks, contact matrices, and regulatory links. Absent means no threshold / unspecified.

name: AccessMethod
description: Description of an access method (i.e. communication protocol) that can be used to fetch a File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of the AccessMethod object of the GA4GH DRS data model.

slots.name: access_protocol
slots.description: Access protocol used to access the File object (orig: DrsObject). Renamed from the FGA-WG slot access_method.

slots.name: access_url
slots.description: AccessURL object providing URL and associated HTTP headers to access the File object (orig: DrsObject).

slots.name: region
slots.description: Name of the region in the cloud service provider that the object belongs to.

name: AccessURL
description: The URL and associated HTTP headers to access the File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of AccessURL object of the GA4GH DRS data model.

slots.name: url
slots.description: A fully resolvable URL that can be used to fetch the actual object bytes.

slots.name: headers
slots.description: An optional list of headers to include in the HTTP request to `url`. These headers can be used to provide auth tokens required to fetch the object bytes.

name: Any
description: The linkml:Any allows the range of a slot to be any object (see https://linkml.io/linkml/schemas/advanced.html#linkml-any-type).

name: AssessmentValue
description: Key-value pair representing a specific value produced by a quality assessment.

slots.name: key
slots.description: Key/name of the assessment value.

slots.name: value
slots.description: Value corresponding to the assessment key.

name: Checksum
description: A checksum of a File object (orig: DrsObject). Exact copy of the Checksum object of the GA4GH DRS data model.

slots.name: checksum_type
slots.description: The digest method used to create the checksum. The value (e.g. `sha-256`) SHOULD be listed as `Hash Name String` in the https://www.iana.org/assignments/named-information/named-information.xhtml#hash-alg [IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry]. Other values MAY be used, as long as implementors are aware of the issues discussed in https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6920#section-9.4 [RFC6920]. GA4GH may provide more explicit guidance for use of non-IANA-registered algorithms in the future. Until then, if implementors do choose such an algorithm (e.g. because it's implemented by their storage provider), they SHOULD use an existing standard `type` value such as `md5`, `etag`, `crc32c`, `trunc512`, or `sha1`.

slots.name: checksum
slots.description: The hex-string encoded checksum for the data.

name: File
description: General information about a particular data file. Most fields (marked with an asterix*) are copied from the GA4GH DRS DrsObject model, which is the top-level object returned from a DRS server in response to a successful lookup call (i.e. https://ga4gh.github.io/data-repository-service-schemas/preview/release/drs-1.4.0/docs/#tag/Objects).

slots.name: file_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the data file (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: access_methods
slots.description: The list of access methods that can be used to fetch the data file.

slots.name: checksums
slots.description: A list of checksums of the data file. For blobs, the checksum is computed over the bytes in the blob.

slots.name: file_input_sources
slots.description: External or internal references to data sources for the file, typically a data collection or a process that has generated the file. Internal references should lead to FileCollection, File, Experiment, or Analysis objects.

slots.name: file_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the data file, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: created_time
slots.description: Timestamp of content creation in RFC3339. (This is the creation time of the underlying content, not of the JSON object.).

slots.name: drs_uri
slots.description: A drs:// hostname-based URI, as defined in the DRS documentation, that tells clients how to access this object. The intent of this field is to make DRS objects self-contained, and therefore easier for clients to store and pass around. For example, if you arrive at this DRS JSON by resolving a compact identifier-based DRS URI, the self_uri presents you with a hostname and properly encoded DRS ID for use in subsequent access endpoint calls.

slots.name: file_description
slots.description: A human readable description of the data file.

slots.name: file_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the data file.

slots.name: file_name
slots.description: A string that can be used to name a data file. This string is made up of uppercase and lowercase letters, decimal digits, hypen, period, and underscore [A-Za-z0-9.-_]. See http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap03.html#tag_03_282 [portable filenames].

slots.name: file_size
slots.description: For blobs, the blob size in bytes.

slots.name: file_type
slots.description: The file format of the data file, as an ontology term. For genomic annotation files the authoritative format is `TrackFormat.file_format` (the ONGA Format vocabulary, reached via `track_format` on GenomicAnnotationFile); `file_type` exists for non-annotation files (e.g. FASTQ) that File also covers.

slots.name: file_version
slots.description: A string representing a version. (Some systems may use checksum, a RFC3339 timestamp, or an incrementing version number.).

slots.name: filecollection_refs
slots.description: Internal references to the FileCollection objects (within the deposit) that contains the data file, if any.

slots.name: mime_type
slots.description: A string providing the mime-type of the data file.

slots.name: quality_assessments
slots.description: An array of QualityAssessment objects containing the main quality scores from assessment techniques applied to the data file.

slots.name: run_provenance
slots.description: Document detailing the provenance of the experiment or analysis run which produced the file as one of its outputs. The provenance info should include software versions, parameter settings, etc.

slots.name: updated_time
slots.description: Timestamp of content update in RFC3339, identical to created_time in systems that do not support updates. (This is the update time of the underlying content, not of the JSON object.).

name: GenomicAnnotationFile
description: Information about a genomic annotation / track file. GenomicAnnotationFile is a specification of the File entity and inherits all the fields defined in File, in addition to the fields that are specific to GenomicAnnotationFile, as detailed here. This is the class that composes the five ONGA descriptor schemas: the required reference_genome (the coordinate system) plus the recommended track_format, track_interpretation, track_provenance, and track_geometry descriptors.

slots.name: file_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the data file (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: reference_genome
slots.description: The reference genome the annotation is defined against, consequently defining the genomic coordinate system for the annotation. Renamed from the FGA-WG slot genome_assembly; the range is the ONGA ReferenceGenome descriptor schema. Required: a genomic annotation without a coordinate system is not a genomic annotation.

slots.name: access_methods
slots.description: The list of access methods that can be used to fetch the data file.

slots.name: checksums
slots.description: A list of checksums of the data file. For blobs, the checksum is computed over the bytes in the blob.

slots.name: file_input_sources
slots.description: External or internal references to data sources for the file, typically a data collection or a process that has generated the file. Internal references should lead to FileCollection, File, Experiment, or Analysis objects.

slots.name: file_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the data file, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: track_format
slots.description: How the track is encoded on disk: the TrackFormat descriptor (file_format drawing on the Format vocabulary, plus BED column conventions).

slots.name: track_geometry
slots.description: Geometric properties of the sequence features in the genomic annotation file if considered as an one-dimensional genome browser track (also relevant for non-visual analyses).

slots.name: track_interpretation
slots.description: What the track content represents: the TrackInterpretation descriptor (output_type / feature_type drawing on the DataType and FeatureType vocabularies, plus the content facets).

slots.name: track_provenance
slots.description: What was done to the data: the TrackProvenance descriptor (processing/derivation facets such as read_multiplicity, filter_status, normalization, thresholding, derivation).

slots.name: created_time
slots.description: Timestamp of content creation in RFC3339. (This is the creation time of the underlying content, not of the JSON object.).

slots.name: drs_uri
slots.description: A drs:// hostname-based URI, as defined in the DRS documentation, that tells clients how to access this object. The intent of this field is to make DRS objects self-contained, and therefore easier for clients to store and pass around. For example, if you arrive at this DRS JSON by resolving a compact identifier-based DRS URI, the self_uri presents you with a hostname and properly encoded DRS ID for use in subsequent access endpoint calls.

slots.name: file_description
slots.description: A human readable description of the data file.

slots.name: file_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the data file.

slots.name: file_name
slots.description: A string that can be used to name a data file. This string is made up of uppercase and lowercase letters, decimal digits, hypen, period, and underscore [A-Za-z0-9.-_]. See http://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap03.html#tag_03_282 [portable filenames].

slots.name: file_size
slots.description: For blobs, the blob size in bytes.

slots.name: file_type
slots.description: The file format of the data file, as an ontology term. For genomic annotation files the authoritative format is `TrackFormat.file_format` (the ONGA Format vocabulary, reached via `track_format` on GenomicAnnotationFile); `file_type` exists for non-annotation files (e.g. FASTQ) that File also covers.

slots.name: file_version
slots.description: A string representing a version. (Some systems may use checksum, a RFC3339 timestamp, or an incrementing version number.).

slots.name: filecollection_refs
slots.description: Internal references to the FileCollection objects (within the deposit) that contains the data file, if any.

slots.name: genomic_annotation_digest
slots.description: Content-derived digest for distributed identification of genomic annotation files. (This field is currently a placeholder, as an algorithm for generating such a digest is yet to be specified.).

slots.name: mime_type
slots.description: A string providing the mime-type of the data file.

slots.name: quality_assessments
slots.description: An array of QualityAssessment objects containing the main quality scores from assessment techniques applied to the data file.

slots.name: run_provenance
slots.description: Document detailing the provenance of the experiment or analysis run which produced the file as one of its outputs. The provenance info should include software versions, parameter settings, etc.

slots.name: updated_time
slots.description: Timestamp of content update in RFC3339, identical to created_time in systems that do not support updates. (This is the update time of the underlying content, not of the JSON object.).

name: InputSource
description: General object representing the source of data files, samples, or other entities used as input to a process or a result. An input source refering to a single file or sample object will represent that item only, while an input source referring to a container or process may represent a number of disctinct input items. InputSource also contains information about the type of relationship, replication labelling, versioning and retrieval date. The qualified_relation values are typically PROV CURIEs (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy, ...) carried as data-level cross-references.

rules.summary: Exactly one of inputsource_external_ref / inputsource_ref is required.

slots.name: qualified_relation
slots.description: A description of the relationship with the input source, typically a PROV CURIE (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:used, ...) carried as a data value.

slots.name: biological_replicate_labels
slots.description: Labels denoting the biological replicates within which the relation is defined, if any.

slots.name: database_accessions
slots.description: Accession numbers for database records used as input source. Used in connection with "inputsource_external_ref".

slots.name: date_of_retrieval
slots.description: Date of retrieval from the input source, typically used to timestamp downloading data from a database or URL.

slots.name: inputsource_external_ref
slots.description: Reference to an external entity as the input source, using a globally unique identifier or an URL. External references will in most cases refer to a database, data record, data file, website or other data source. One of "inputsource_external_ref" or "inputsource_ref" must be specified.

slots.name: inputsource_ref
slots.description: Reference to an internal object as the input source using a local identifier. Entities to be used as an internal input source includes FileCollection, Sample, Experiment, Analysis or File as restricted by the description of the field where the input source is used. One of "inputsource_external_ref" or "inputsource_ref" must be specified.

slots.name: technical_replicate_labels
slots.description: Labels denoting the technical replicates within which the relation is defined, if any.

slots.name: version
slots.description: Version information for the retrieval from the input source.

name: QualityAssessment
description: Represents the results of a quality assessment that has been carried out on a data file resulting from an experiment or analysis. This is the natural home for repository QC metrics (e.g. BEDbase BedStats numbers). A typed QC vocabulary may later tighten assessment_method; for now it accepts a free string or a Term.

slots.name: assessment_method
slots.description: Quality assessment method that has been carried out (e.g. BUSCO, OMArk, peak calling statistics, etc.)

slots.name: assessment_values
slots.description: Main values produced by the quality assessment.

slots.name: assessment_details_url
slots.description: URL to a report containing the detailed output from the quality assessment.

name: Term
description: Helper entity to represent an ontology term as a data value. Term instances are DATA-LEVEL cross-references: a CURIE carried inside a record, never a schema-level IRI. Schema-level cross-references use mapping slots (exact_mappings/close_mappings/broad_mappings) per ONGA design principle #7, never `meaning:`.

slots.name: id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the ontology term (in CURIE form).

slots.name: label
slots.description: Human-readable label associated to the term id in the current version of the ontology (as listed in the "ontology_versions" field of the Deposit object).

name: Analysis
description: Represents the computational processing applied to data from a sequencing experiment, or from another analysis. This can be described at the level of individual analysis steps in a workflow/pipeline, or more generally for the workflow/pipeline as a whole. Boundary with TrackProvenance: TrackProvenance (Layer 2) carries faceted, closed-vocabulary descriptors of what was done to the CONTENT (read selection, filtering, normalization, ...); Analysis is the record of the ACTIVITY itself (workflow, tool, version, inputs). Complementary, not competing.

slots.name: analysis_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the analysis (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: analysis_input_sources
slots.description: External or internal references to the data sources used as input to the analysis.

slots.name: analysis_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the analysis, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: analysis_type
slots.description: The type of analysis carried out.

slots.name: analysis_description
slots.description: Human-readable description of the analysis.

slots.name: analysis_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the analysis.

slots.name: analysis_main_tool
slots.description: Main software tool used for the analysis.

slots.name: analysis_main_tool_version
slots.description: Version of the main software tool used for the analysis.

slots.name: analysis_protocol
slots.description: Document describing the analysis protocol that was followed.

slots.name: analysis_study_ref
slots.description: Internal reference to the study within which the analysis has been carried out.

slots.name: analysis_workflow
slots.description: External reference to the analysis workflow, with availability in at least one machine-operable form (e.g. CWL, Nextflow, ...).

name: Contact
description: Contact information for a person or an organisation.

slots.name: name
slots.description: Name of the person or organisation.

slots.name: contact_id
slots.description: Globally unique identifier for a person (e.g. ORCID ID) or organisation (e.g. BioProject accession).

slots.name: email
slots.description: E-mail address of the person or organisation.

name: Deposit
description: Information about a public deposit of a document containing metadata about a set of genome annotation files.

slots.name: deposit_versioned_id
slots.description: A globally unique, persistent and versioned identifier for the public deposit of the metadata document. A versioned DOI to a deposited document is recommended.

slots.name: deposit_first_created
slots.description: The date and time of the creation of the first deposited version of the metadata document.

slots.name: deposit_id
slots.description: A globally unique and persistent identifier for the public deposit of the metadata document. A DOI or other persistent identifier is recommended.

slots.name: deposit_last_changed
slots.description: The date and time of the last deposited change of the current metadata document (corresponding to "deposit_versioned_id").

name: Document
description: Information about a document containing metadata about a set of genome annotation files, harmonised according to this schema. This includes self-referential identifiers and versioning of public deposits of the document.

slots.name: document_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the metadata document, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: document_ontology_versions
slots.description: Map from the version-agnostic URL to a versioned URL (e.g. "versionIRI" in owl) of each ontology used in the current metadata deposit (corresponding to deposit_versioned_id").

slots.name: document_deposit
slots.description: Information about the public deposit of the metadata document.

slots.name: document_description
slots.description: Human-readable description of the metadata document.

slots.name: document_input_sources
slots.description: References to other input sources from which this entire metadata document was derived, or possibly including DOIs of other metadata documents used as source.

name: Donor
description: Information about the donor or complete organism from which the sample was taken.

slots.name: donor_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the donor/organism (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: species_taxon
slots.description: Taxonomical classification of the species of the donor/organism.

slots.name: donor_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the donor/organism.

slots.name: donor_sex
slots.description: Biological sex of the donor/organism (the SAMPLE side of the crucial sample-sex vs reference-build-sex distinction, ONGA design principle #5). Do not confuse with ReferenceGenome.build_sex, which records which sex chromosomes the reference ASSEMBLY contains. Renamed from the FGA-WG slot sex.

name: Experiment
description: Represents a sequencing experiment that has been carried out within a study, based on biological samples, and providing data files as output. Subsequent analysis of output data is described by the Analysis entity. Assay properties (assay_type, antibody_target, instrument, ...) live HERE, on the investigation-layer Experiment record — not in the ONGA content vocabularies, consistent with ONGA design principle #5 (sample and assay properties are out of scope for the content vocabularies).

slots.name: experiment_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the experiment (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: assay_type
slots.description: Sequencing technique intended for this library.

slots.name: experiment_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the experiment, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: experiment_samples
slots.description: External or internal references to samples used in the experiment. Internal references should refer to Sample objects.

slots.name: experiment_study_ref
slots.description: Internal reference to the study within which the experiment has been carried out.

slots.name: molecule_type
slots.description: Specifies the type of source material that is being sequenced.

slots.name: antibody_target
slots.description: The target of the antibody used in the experiment.

slots.name: biological_processes
slots.description: Biological processes illuminated by the experiment.

slots.name: design_description
slots.description: The high-level experiment design including layout, protocol.

slots.name: experiment_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the experiment.

slots.name: instrument
slots.description: Technology platform used to perform nucleic acid sequencing, including name and/or number associated with a specific sequencing instrument model. It is recommended to be as specific as possible for this property (e.g. if the model/revision are available, providing that instead of just the instrument maker).

slots.name: library_layout
slots.description: Whether the library was built as paired-end, or single-end.

slots.name: sequencing_protocol
slots.description: Set of rules which guides how the sequencing protocol was followed. Change-tracking services such as Protocol.io or GitHub are encouraged instead of dumping free text in this field.

name: FileCollection
description: A collection of files, according to some selection criteria. Mainly intended for GenomicAnnotationFile entities, but other types of files can also be contained in a collection, e.g. raw data files such as FASTQ files. This is the natural future home for the BEDset concept (a curated collection of BED files).

slots.name: filecollection_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the file collection (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: deposit_versioned_ref
slots.description: Reference to versioned id of deposit containing this file collection.

slots.name: filecollection_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the file collection, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: contact
slots.description: Contact point for the parent object (e.g. the study, or the creator/maintainer of a file collection).

slots.name: filecollection_description
slots.description: Human-readable description of the file collection.

slots.name: filecollection_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the file collection (in most cases, this will not exist).

slots.name: filecollection_input_sources
slots.description: References to other input sources from which this file collection was derived.

name: OntologyVersions
description: Information about an ontology used in the metadata: a map from the version-agnostic URL to a versioned URL. Version pinning is real work for deposit documents — the OWL versionIRI mechanism serves the same purpose at the ontology level.

slots.name: namespace
slots.description: The CURIE namespace (prefix) an ontology (e.g. "GO" for Gene Ontology).

slots.name: ontology_url
slots.description: The version-agnostic URL of the ontology (e.g. the IRI of the ontology in OWL).

slots.name: versioned_ontology_url
slots.description: The versioned URL of the ontology (e.g. the "versionIRI" in OWL).

name: Sample
description: Information about a biospecimen/sample used as raw material for lab experiments. Sample properties are ontology-delegated via Term-valued slots (UBERON for tissue, CL for cell type, CLO for cell line, PATO for phenotype), per ONGA design principle #5.

rules.summary: When biospecimen_classification = "in vitro differentiated cells" or biospecimen_classification = "primary cell": cell_type required.
When biospecimen_classification = "tissue" or biospecimen_classification = "organoid": organism_tissue required.

slots.name: sample_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the biospecimen/sample (unique within the metadata deposit).

slots.name: biospecimen_classification
slots.description: Main type of structural unit to be used for classification of the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: donor_organism_ref
slots.description: Internal reference to the donor/organism from which the biospecimen/sample was taken.

slots.name: sample_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: sample_label
slots.description: A human-readable description of the sample, short enough to be used for listings within software user interfaces, tables, illustration legends, etc.

slots.name: cell_line
slots.description: Cultured cell line used in the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: cell_type
slots.description: Cell type of isolated normal cells in the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: donor_age
slots.description: Age of the donor/organism at the time of sampling

slots.name: donor_clinical_information
slots.description: Clinical information of the donor/organism at the time of sampling.

slots.name: donor_development_stage
slots.description: Development stage of the donor at the time of sampling.

slots.name: organism_tissue
slots.description: Part of organism (typically tissue or organ) from which the biospecimen/sample was taken, or cell line was derived from. UBERON range; this is the organism_part landing slot anticipated by mappings/scope_delegations.tsv.

slots.name: other_biospecimen
slots.description: Other biospecimen-related terms that can be used to further classify the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: phenotype
slots.description: Main phenotype (e.g. disease) connected to the biospecimen/sample.

slots.name: sample_collection_date
slots.description: Date of sample collection.

slots.name: sample_collection_location
slots.description: Geographical location where the sample was collected.

slots.name: sample_description
slots.description: Human-readable description of the biospecimen/sample and the sampling process.

slots.name: sampling_protocol
slots.description: Protocol detailing the collection and treatment of the biospecimen/sample.

name: Study
description: A scientific study, i.e. a unit of research, within which experiments and/or analyses have been carried out.

slots.name: study_id
slots.description: Internal identifier for the study (unique within the metadata deposit). Namespace: "study".

slots.name: study_title
slots.description: Title of the study.

slots.name: contact
slots.description: Contact point for the parent object (e.g. the study, or the creator/maintainer of a file collection).

slots.name: project_external_ref
slots.description: Reference to a project within which the study was carried out (preferably a BioProject CURIE).

slots.name: project_name
slots.description: Name of the project within which the study was carried out.

slots.name: publications
slots.description: List of (relevant) publications containing the results of the study (in the form of DOI CURIEs).

slots.name: study_abstract
slots.description: Abstract of the study.

slots.name: study_external_id
slots.description: External, globally unique identifier for the study (preferably a BioStudies CURIE).

name: TopLevel
description: A document of harmonised metadata for a set of genome annotation files. This is the top-level class to be used as root for a metadata deposit document.

slots.name: document
slots.description: Information about this document containing harmonised metadata about a set of genome annotation files. This includes self-referential identifiers and versioning of public deposits of the document.

slots.name: analyses
slots.description: Information about computational processing and analyses that have been carried out to generate the files.

slots.name: donors
slots.description: Information about the donors or complete organisms from which the samples were taken.

slots.name: experiments
slots.description: Information about sequencing experiments that have been carried out to generate the files.

slots.name: file_collections
slots.description: Information about collections of files contained in this dataset, each collection defined according to some selection criteria.

slots.name: files
slots.description: Information about particular genome annotation (and other relevant) files.

slots.name: samples
slots.description: Information about the biospecimens/samples used as raw material for lab experiments.
